Generation of Hamiltonian and Overlap Matrices

This tutorial explains how to prepare electronic data for QTrans using the nonmagnetic aluminum (Al) and ferromagnetic iron (Fe) as examples. QTrans stores the structure, orbital basis, Hamiltonian, and overlap matrices in graph data, written as graph_data_QTrans.npz by graph-pack. Tutorial data directories may rename this file to graph_data.npz.

Paths below are relative to the tutorial repository root. Run graph packing from the relevant graph-packing directory so that relative paths in the YAML configuration resolve correctly. Each example includes a ref/ directory with previously generated inputs and outputs for comparison. The QTrans YAML configurations below are shown in full, with machine-specific paths replaced by /path/to/... placeholders. Omitted optional parameters use the program defaults.

Based on DFT Calculations

1. OpenMX: Al as the main example

Install OpenMX and obtain the read_openmx matrix-export executable from the HamGNN repository. QTrans invokes read_openmx to extract Hamiltonian and overlap matrices from OpenMX binary outputs into a temporary HS.json file. The separate openmx_postprocess executable is needed for the HamGNN preprocessing route described later; it is not required for packing the SCF matrices in these examples.

For detailed DFT parameter settings and instructions on using OpenMX, refer to the manuals on the official OpenMX website. The steps below focus on generating and converting the outputs needed by QTrans.

The example is located in tutorials/Al/openmx/graph-pack/. Its ref/ directory contains outputs for reference.

Step 1. Prepare the executables and input

Before running the example:

  • Update DATA.PATH in DFT/openmx_Al.dat to your OpenMX pseudopotential and atomic-orbital data directory.

  • Update software_path.openmx_read_path in input_graph.yaml to an executable read_openmx.

  • Make sure openmx is available in your shell, or use its full path in the command below.

The supplied input uses the GGA-PBE functional, the Al7.0-s2p2d1 orbital basis, and the Al_PBE19 pseudopotential without spin polarization. It sets scf.energycutoff to 200 Ry, scf.Kgrid to 18 18 18, scf.ElectronicTemperature to 300 K, and scf.criterion to 1.0e-12 Hartree. Keep HS.fileout on enabled to write the binary Hamiltonian and overlap data required by QTrans. Check convergence before applying these settings to another system.

Step 2. Run the self-consistent calculation

From the repository root, run:

cd tutorials/Al/openmx/graph-pack/DFT/
mpirun -np 8 openmx openmx_Al.dat > openmx_scf.out
cd ..

The input sets System.Name to crystal, so the files needed for graph packing are DFT/crystal.scfout and DFT/crystal.out. openmx_scf.out is the redirected terminal output; it is distinct from crystal.out, which QTrans reads for structure and convergence information. Check that the SCF calculation converged before continuing.

Step 3. Configure graph packing

The complete input_graph.yaml is:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'graph-pack'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_read_path: ./read_openmx

material:
  nao_max: 14
  DFT_software: openmx

graph_pack:
  HSout_filename: 'crystal.scfout'
  vbout_filename: 'crystal.out'
  data_folder: ./DFT/
  converge_step_ratio: 0.9

Replace the executable path with your installation path. nao_max selects the orbital definition used to pack the data and must match the electronic-structure setup. This DFT example uses 14 for the aluminum basis used here. A larger atomic-orbital basis can improve accuracy at a higher computational cost. Set nao_max to match the basis used in the DFT calculation; increasing this parameter alone does not improve accuracy.

HSout_filename identifies the binary matrix file, and vbout_filename identifies the OpenMX text output. data_folder selects the calculation folders. For multiple calculations, it can be a glob pattern such as ./DFT/*/; folders missing required files are reported and skipped.

The parameter converge_step_ratio filters calculations using their SCF iteration count relative to scf.maxIter. The example uses 0.9. This filter supplements checking the SCF convergence and does not set the convergence tolerance of OpenMX.

Step 4. Pack and inspect the result

From tutorials/Al/openmx/graph-pack/, run:

QTrans_prep --config input_graph.yaml > graph_pack.out

The output is graph_data_QTrans.npz in basic.outdir. Check that graph_pack.out reports one useful folder and successful completion. Reference files are available at:

ref/
  DFT/crystal.scfout
  DFT/crystal.out
  DFT/openmx_scf.out
  graph_data_QTrans.npz
  graph_pack.out

Reference logs may contain paths from the original calculation environment; use the paths shown above for the current directory layout.

For unit-cell calculations, provide the generated dataset through basic.graph_data_path_uc in the calculator configuration. To prepare EPC from displaced-supercell data, continue with EPC Gradient Matrix Preparation.

Warning

QTrans creates and removes HS.json in each selected calculation folder during matrix extraction. Use folders without an existing HS.json and avoid concurrent graph-packing jobs in the same folders.

2. OpenMX: magnetic Fe

The bcc Fe example is located in tutorials/Fe/openmx/graph-pack/. Follow the same SCF and graph-packing sequence as for Al, with the changes below.

Spin-polarized DFT input

Update DATA.PATH in DFT/openmx_Fe.dat. The supplied input uses Fe5.5H-s3p2d1 and Fe_PBE19H, a 200 Ry cutoff, a 22 x 22 x 22 k-point mesh, and scf.criterion: 1.0e-10 Hartree. Its key magnetic settings are:

scf.SpinPolarization    on
HS.fileout             on

<Atoms.SpeciesAndCoordinates
  1  Fe  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000  10.00  6.00  on
Atoms.SpeciesAndCoordinates>

The unequal initial spin populations seed a magnetic state; they do not specify the final converged magnetic moment. Check both SCF convergence and the resulting magnetic state in crystal.out. This example treats collinear magnetism without spin-orbit coupling.

Matching graph-packing settings

The complete Fe input_graph.yaml is shown below. Its magnetic setting is the main difference from the Al configuration:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'graph-pack'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_read_path: ./read_openmx

material:
  nao_max: 14
  DFT_software: openmx
  magnetic_type: collinear # Fe is ferromagnetic!

graph_pack:
  HSout_filename: 'crystal.scfout'
  vbout_filename: 'crystal.out'
  data_folder: ./DFT/
  converge_step_ratio: 0.9

magnetic_type: collinear tells QTrans to retain the two spin channels. It must match scf.SpinPolarization on in the DFT calculation; the default nonmagnetic setting used for Al is not appropriate for this Fe dataset. nao_max: 14 selects the OpenMX orbital definition, which includes the Fe basis used here. See Atomic Orbital Basis Definition and Valence Electron Counts for the orbital and electron-count definitions.

From the tutorial repository root, run:

cd tutorials/Fe/openmx/graph-pack/DFT/
mpirun -np 8 openmx openmx_Fe.dat > openmx.out
cd ..
QTrans_prep --config input_graph.yaml > graph.out

Set software_path.openmx_read_path to your matrix-export executable before packing. The output is graph_data_QTrans.npz; compare it and graph.out with the corresponding files in ref/. The reference log reports Dealing with a COLLINEAR magnetic system. and one useful folder. For subsequent transport property calculations, keep advanced.magnetic_type: collinear and the no-SOC setting consistent with this prepared dataset.

3. ABACUS: the Al workflow

For detailed DFT parameter settings and instructions on using ABACUS, refer to the official ABACUS documentation. The steps below focus on generating and converting the outputs needed by QTrans.

The example is located in tutorials/Al/abacus/graph-pack/. Reference outputs are provided in tutorials/Al/abacus/graph-pack/ref/.

Step 1. Prepare the ABACUS input

The DFT/ directory contains INPUT, STRU, and KPT for an LCAO self-consistent calculation of aluminum. The overall sequence is the same as for OpenMX: run DFT, locate the matrix outputs, then run QTrans_prep. ABACUS supplies CSR matrices that QTrans reads directly, so no read_openmx conversion is needed. Before running:

  • Update pseudo_dir and orbital_dir in INPUT to your local pseudopotential and numerical-orbital directories.

  • Ensure that these directories contain Al_ONCV_PBE-1.0.upf and Al_gga_7au_100Ry_4s4p1d.orb, respectively, as specified in STRU.

  • Make the abacus executable available in your shell. If using the supplied sub_abacus submission script, adapt its scheduler settings, modules, and executable path to your cluster.

The key settings in INPUT are:

suffix          Al
basis_type      lcao
calculation     scf
out_mat_hs2     1

out_mat_hs2 enables the real-space Hamiltonian and overlap matrix output required for graph packing. With suffix set to Al, ABACUS writes these files to OUT.Al/. The supplied input uses an energy cutoff of 150 Ry, scf_thr: 1e-9, 10 bands, Gaussian smearing with smearing_sigma: 0.01, and a Gamma-centered 10 x 10 x 10 k-point mesh. These settings describe this example; check convergence for your own system.

Step 2. Run the self-consistent calculation

From the repository root, run:

cd tutorials/Al/abacus/graph-pack/DFT/
mpirun -np 16 abacus > abacus.out
cd ..

Check SCF convergence in DFT/OUT.Al/running_scf.log. Graph packing requires the original DFT/STRU and the following output files:

DFT/OUT.Al/
  running_scf.log
  data-HR-sparse_SPIN0.csr
  data-SR-sparse_SPIN0.csr

Step 3. Configure graph packing

From tutorials/Al/abacus/graph-pack/, configure input_graph.yaml as follows, replacing the data-directory paths with your local paths:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'graph-pack'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  abacus_dftdata_dir: /path/to/SG15_ONCV
  abacus_orb_dir: /path/to/SG15-std

material:
  nao_max: 40
  DFT_software: abacus

graph_pack:
  data_folder: ./DFT
  abacus_out_folder: OUT.Al
  abacus_scf_log: running_scf.log

The supplied data_folder: ./DFT is equivalent to ./DFT/ above. abacus_out_folder is relative to each selected calculation folder and must match the ABACUS output directory. abacus_scf_log identifies the log inside that directory.

nao_max: 40 selects QTrans’s ABACUS orbital definition for this example; it is not the number of orbitals on each atom. Keep this definition consistent with the numerical orbitals used in the DFT calculation. QTrans reads the ABACUS CSR matrices directly.

Step 4. Pack and inspect the result

Run from tutorials/Al/abacus/graph-pack/:

QTrans_prep --config input_graph.yaml > graph.out

The resulting graph_data_QTrans.npz is written to basic.outdir and can be supplied through basic.graph_data_path_uc for unit-cell calculations. Compare with ref/graph.out and ref/graph_data_QTrans.npz in this graph-pack/ directory. The reference directory also includes the DFT inputs and the required OUT.Al files.

Based on HamGNN Prediction with OpenMX

We can also predict the Hamiltonian using HamGNN. The prediction example is located in tutorials/Al/openmx/predict-HamGNN/. It uses the universal Hamiltonian model [9], available from Zenodo.

Prepare graph data for prediction

The prediction route first constructs graph data containing the structure, overlap matrices, and non-self-consistent Hamiltonian contribution. HamGNN then predicts the Hamiltonian using this graph data and the universal model.

From the repository root, enter the DFT directory:

cd tutorials/Al/openmx/predict-HamGNN/DFT/

Update DATA.PATH in openmx_Al.dat and ensure that openmx_postprocess and read_openmx are compatible with your OpenMX installation. Obtain these tools from the HamGNN project and place the executables in this DFT directory, or update the command and configuration to use their installation paths.

Run the preprocessing command:

mpirun -np 1 ./openmx_postprocess openmx_Al.dat > openmx_nonscf.out

This step produces overlap.scfout. The graph-packing configuration uses DFT_software: openmx and nao_max: 26 to match the universal model’s orbital definition. The complete input_graph.yaml is:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'graph-pack'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_read_path: ./read_openmx

material:
  nao_max: 26
  DFT_software: openmx

graph_pack:
  HSout_filename: null
  vbout_filename: null
  nonscf_filename: overlap.scfout
  stdin_filename: openmx_Al.dat
  data_folder: ./

Here, stdin_filename supplies the structure and basis information from the OpenMX input. Use YAML null for disabled filenames, and leave vbout_filename unset or null to select the non-SCF graph-packing route. Set software_path.openmx_read_path to the local ./read_openmx or another compatible executable.

From this DFT directory, pack the data and copy it to the filename expected by HamGNN:

QTrans_prep --config input_graph.yaml > graph_pack.out
cp graph_data_QTrans.npz graph_data.npz

HamGNN expects graph_data.npz in the directory specified by dataset_params.graph_data_path. The supplied predict/HamGNN_config.yaml sets this path to ../DFT/. Previously generated preprocessing outputs are available in predict-HamGNN/ref/DFT/.

Prediction configuration

Before running inference, update setup.checkpoint_path in predict/HamGNN_config.yaml to the downloaded model and use a compatible HamGNN environment. This Al example selects setup.stage: test, output_nets.HamGNN_out.nao_max: 26, and add_H0: True. Keep the model, orbital definition, graph data, and non-self-consistent contribution consistent.

Run the prediction from the predict directory:

cd ../predict/
HamGNN2.0 --config HamGNN_config.yaml > HamGNN_test.out

The predicted Hamiltonian is written to version_0/prediction_hamiltonian.npy for the reference run. Reference outputs are provided in predict-HamGNN/ref/predict/, including HamGNN_test.out and the prediction file. The output version directory may change for subsequent runs.

Use the predicted Hamiltonian together with the corresponding graph data; the structures, ordering, and orbital basis must match. For EPC gradient preparation, set grad_epc.use_prediction: True and supply the prediction through grad_epc.pred_H_sc_path together with matching supercell graph data and mapping, as described in EPC Gradient Matrix Preparation.

The prediction example above is for nonmagnetic Al. The magnetic Fe example in this tutorial uses spin-polarized DFT data; applying a model to Fe requires a model and graph representation compatible with that magnetic configuration.

For HamGNN installation and inference details, consult the HamGNN documentation.

Note

The graph-pack mode of QTrans_prep supports MPI parallel execution across multiple calculation folders, including displaced supercells. Each rank builds the graphs for its assigned folders; rank 0 gathers, sorts, and saves all graphs in a single output file. Each rank may process one or more folders, depending on the number of folders and MPI ranks.

For multiple folders selected by graph_pack.data_folder, you can run:

mpirun -np 4 QTrans_prep --config input_graph.yaml > graph_pack.out

A single folder is processed by one rank, so the single-folder examples above use a single process. Gradient matrix generation with grad-epc is performed on rank 0 and does not benefit from MPI parallel execution.

Passing unit-cell data to the calculator

The calculation tutorials read data/graph_data.npz within each material/software directory. Graph packing writes graph_data_QTrans.npz; renaming the copied file does not change its contents. For example, after completing the OpenMX Al graph-packing calculation, run from the tutorial repository root:

cp -i tutorials/Al/openmx/graph-pack/graph_data_QTrans.npz tutorials/Al/openmx/data/graph_data.npz

The -i option asks before replacing supplied example data. To preserve those data, keep your generated file in a separate directory and update basic.graph_data_path_uc in the complete calculator YAML instead. The same handoff applies to OpenMX Fe and ABACUS Al, using their respective material/software directories. Copy the unit-cell dataset, not the graph containing the displaced supercells.

For the prediction route, use the graph and predicted Hamiltonian files specified in the prediction section above; copying a graph alone does not substitute the predicted Hamiltonian. Continue with EPC Gradient Matrix Preparation for gradient data and Phonon Force Data Preparation for phonon force data.
